title: Michael W. Charney, A History of Modern Burma
note: The standard single-volume scholarly history, running from the fall of the Konbaung dynasty to 2008. Used here as the general spine for the colonial and post-independence chapters.

title: Angelene Naw, Aung San and the Struggle for Burmese Independence
note: Biography built on British archival records and interviews. The detailed source for Aung San, the Thakin movement and the independence negotiations. Also readable at archive.org/details/aungsanstrugglef0000nawa.

title: Mary P. Callahan, Making Enemies: War and State Building in Burma
note: Argues the army's dominance grew out of war and state formation between 1826 and 1962. Callahan was the first researcher given access to the Burmese military archives, which is why this is the reference for how the Tatmadaw became the state.

title: Thant Myint-U, The Hidden History of Burma
note: Account of the 2011-2020 opening and its collapse, by a historian who worked inside the reform process. Partisan in the sense that the author was a participant, and read here as informed testimony rather than neutral survey.

title: Emergence of the Dobama Asiayone and the Thakins
note: Open-access study of how the Dobama Asiayone formed and why its members adopted the title Thakin. Establishes the movement's origins and composition.

title: Nick Cheesman, How in Myanmar 'National Races' Came to Surpass Citizenship and Exclude Rohingya
note: Shows that taingyintha ('national races') as a political category is a relatively recent invention that the post-1962 state made the basis of citizenship. This is the analytical source for the 1982 law. Paywalled.

title: Panglong Agreement, 12 February 1947
note: The agreement text itself. Establishes exactly what was signed and by whom -- which is the point, because what Panglong is remembered as promising is considerably more than what it says.

title: Crackdown: Repression of the 2007 Popular Protests in Burma
note: Documents the August 2007 fuel price rise, the protests that followed, and the crackdown on them.

title: The Day Three Myanmar Banknotes Suddenly Became Worthless
note: Account of the 5 September 1987 demonetisation, which voided the 25, 35 and 75 kyat notes without compensation. The Irrawaddy is an exile-founded outlet, long critical of the military.

publisher: Sciences Po, Mass Violence and Resistance Research Network
title: The repression of the 8-8-88 uprising in Burma/Myanmar
note: Scholarly reconstruction of the August 1988 crackdown. Explicit that no agreed death toll exists.

title: Myanmar country overview and economic monitoring
note: Source for growth averaging about 6 per cent a year from 2011 to 2019, and for the roughly 18 per cent contraction in the year following the coup.

title: GDP growth (annual %) - Myanmar
note: The underlying annual series. Myanmar's national accounts are weak and post-2021 figures are estimates built on limited reporting, so the shape of the curve is more reliable than any single year.

title: Myanmar Opens Its Mobile Phone Market
note: Reports SIM cards falling from over 2,000 US dollars to 1.50 after the 2013 licensing of Telenor and Ooredoo. The single clearest consumer-level measure of what liberalisation changed.

publisher: Republic of the Union of Myanmar
title: Constitution of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar (2008)
note: Primary text. Establishes the reserved military seats, the three security ministries and the amendment threshold.

publisher: Government of Myanmar and signatory ethnic armed organisations
title: Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement
note: Primary text. Establishes who signed and what was agreed; it does not establish who was excluded or why.

publisher: Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw / National Unity Consultative Council
title: Federal Democracy Charter
note: Primary text of the post-coup opposition's constitutional framework. States intentions and structures, not their implementation.

title: Briefing Paper: Effective Control in Myanmar
note: Assesses territorial control by township with an explicit methodology. Produced by a body sympathetic to the opposition, which is why its figures appear here as one assessment among several rather than as settled fact.

title: Myanmar country analysis
note: Ongoing reporting on the armed conflict, the resistance organisations and regional diplomacy.

title: Reports on the human rights situation in Myanmar
note: UN human rights reporting, including post-coup documentation.

publisher: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
title: Myanmar Humanitarian Update
note: Displacement and humanitarian access figures. Figures are periodically revised, so any number taken from here must carry its as-of date.

title: Rohingya emergency
note: Registered refugee populations in Bangladesh.

title: Application of the Genocide Convention (The Gambia v. Myanmar)
note: Case record. Establishes the existence and procedural history of the proceedings, not findings on the merits.

title: Daily briefing and post-coup casualty documentation
note: The most-cited running tally of post-coup killings and detentions. AAPP counts only cases it can verify, so its figures are explicitly a documented floor rather than an estimate of the total.

publisher: Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project
title: Myanmar conflict event data
note: Records that a conflict event occurred at a location. It does NOT establish who controls that location, and is not used here to infer control.

title: Myanmar Conflict Map
note: Territorial control assessment with a published methodology and its own stated uncertainty.

publisher: Institute for Strategy and Policy - Myanmar
title: Myanmar research and analysis
note: Myanmar-based research on governance, administration and the post-coup political landscape.

title: Myanmar electoral and constitutional analysis
note: Electoral system and constitutional process analysis.

title: Myanmar 1990 election and elected parliamentarians
note: Records the NLD winning 392 of 485 declared seats and the authorities' refusal to transfer power or convene the elected parliament.

title: Announcement 34/2026: Secured votes in the 2025 multiparty general election
note: Official results published through the state-run Global New Light of Myanmar. Used for the commission's vote totals and geographic scope, not as independent validation of the election.

title: Myanmar's military-backed party wins election amid opposition exclusion
note: Independent account of the election conditions, opposition exclusion, areas without voting and the continuing constitutional military bloc.

title: Resistance Forces' Control Areas Expanded After Operation 1027
note: Estimates that 39.34 per cent of national landmass was outside Myanmar Armed Forces control. The figure is a dated assessment, not a live territorial ledger.

title: Myanmar civil war simplified.svg
note: CC0 community-maintained cartography used as a dated visual reference for the closing map. Its revision history and source discussions are part of the evidence and the map should not be treated as authoritative.

title: M 7.7 - 2025 Mandalay, Burma (Myanmar) Earthquake
note: Primary event parameters and impact compilation: epicentre, depth, intensity, confirmed surface rupture and the casualty, injury and missing-person totals used here.

title: Myanmar Economic Monitor: Economic Aftershocks
note: Estimates 17 million people affected, nine million severely, more than 207,000 displaced, and US$11 billion in direct physical damage, equivalent to 14 per cent of GDP.

publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
title: International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship (IBTrACS)
note: The merged global best-track archive used for the simplified Cyclone Nargis path. The interface deliberately samples the track and does not infer the storm's wind field or damage footprint from it.

title: The 2020 Myanmar General Elections: Democracy Under Attack
note: Final observation report. Records 396 NLD seats and 33 USDP seats among 476 elected Union Parliament seats, alongside cancellations and wider electoral shortcomings.

title: Preliminary Statement on the 2020 Myanmar General Elections
note: Observers assessed election day positively at most polling stations visited and reported no major irregularities, while identifying serious structural and procedural shortcomings.

title: Situation of human rights in Myanmar
note: Documents the Three Brotherhood Alliance offensive in northern Shan and distinguishes it from the Arakan Army campaign in Rakhine and Paletwa.

title: Hugh Tinker, The Union of Burma: A Study of the First Years of Independence
note: Near-contemporary survey used for the broad 1948 and 1953 insurgent-activity reconstructions. Its maps are interpretive snapshots, not surveyed front lines.

publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
title: The Current Situation in Burma
note: Contemporary U.S. intelligence estimate identifying the CPB, KNDO and PVO remnants as principal insurgent forces and noting government recovery of the main population centres.

publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
title: Probable Developments in Burma Through 1953
note: Contemporary estimate of Communist, Karen and Chinese Nationalist capabilities. Used to check the 1953 actor framing, not to claim exact territorial borders.

title: Jacques P. Leider, Violence and Belonging: Conflict, War, and Insecurity in Arakan, 1942–1952
note: Historical study of wartime and early post-independence violence in Arakan, including the Mujahid movement from 1948.

title: Burma1948.png
note: CC BY-SA 4.0 reconstruction by BorysMapping based on Hugh Tinker's 1957 study. The site redraws its broad activity areas in native SVG and labels their uncertainty.

title: Burma1953.png
note: CC BY-SA 4.0 reconstruction by BorysMapping based on Hugh Tinker's 1957 study. The site redraws its broad activity areas in native SVG and labels their uncertainty.

title: Historical Notes on Burma / Myanmar
note: Used for U Nu’s absence, the attempt at his home, and the reconstitution of the Executive Council after the assassination.

title: The Death of Aung San in 1947 — An Important Clarification
note: Detailed review of the assassination record and Galon U Saw’s conviction.

publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
title: Telegram from Rangoon, 19 July 1947
note: Contemporary diplomatic report identifying U Ohn Maung as Deputy Secretary of Transport and Communications and recording his death.

publisher: Institute of Developing Economies, Japan External Trade Organization
title: Burma/Myanmar political chronology and historical studies
note: Used for the post-assassination political and military leadership context.

title: Burma to Myanmar: large print exhibition guide
note: Summarises Britain’s three-stage annexation in 1824–26, 1852 and 1885.

publisher: Asia Peacebuilding Initiatives, Sasakawa Peace Foundation
title: A ceasefire, an election, a new government: Progress towards peace in Myanmar
note: Retrospective account and ceremony photograph used for the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement signing in Naypyitaw.
